dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Lira! You're being moved to the pit.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: 'Just put in the time and you won't have to work the pit anymore.'

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: At this point I think Kip is lying to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You'd think a year would be long enough to earn some respect around here.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Watch your head.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You act like I've never done this before.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Enough with the attitude, keep it moving!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Am I really working alone again?

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Yes. Now, since I've gotten a bunch of complaints that you can't do your job, show me you still remember.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Go pick up that heat unit over there.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Good, you still remember how to use your arms.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Now hold tthe heat unit in your hands and break it for warmth.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You want to teach me how to walk again or can I get back to work?

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: (agreeing grunt)

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I'll get out of this mine someday.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira, what are those?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: There was an explosion in the mine today so I dec...

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Why did you bring those home!?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Because I'm sick of cold and saw an opportunity, so I took it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira, do you know what the council would do to you if they found out you took them?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I'm just so tired of doing everything the way the council tells us to do it!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: We provide light. We provide heat. You can rely on us.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When has that ever been true?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: You say that but they are the ONLY reason you're able to live your life.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Without them and the tower our planet would be a frozen wasteland, like outside the walls.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yeah, well if my mom were here, she'd be on my side.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Don't pretend you knew who she was.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Well maybe I would know more about her if you didn't pretend she never existed!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: My whole life, I've heard the same thing from everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: 'Your mother was wonderful.'

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: 'Your mother was so kind.'

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: 'Your mother was a genius.'

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When am I going to get a real answer, and not one you'd give to a six-year-old?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: You're right...

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: It's about time you knew the truth about your mother.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Your mother wasn't born in the out skirts. Neither was I for that matter... we both grew up in the Core.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara gre up in a wealthy family that lived near the top of the Core

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: As she got older, Clara found an interest in science, fascinated by the tower and how it could sustain life after centuries without a real sun.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This led her to pursue science and further her education.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara met your father, Reginald Brown this way.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: They were inseparable; studying, partying, you name it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Her success in school allowed her to land a job working in the Primary Tower Lab as soon as she graduated.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara became the youngest person to ever work in the tower, alongside the best scientists in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This is where I met her: Tasked with guarding the door to her lab, I got to see her everyday and we grew close.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: One night, Clara was workinf late and made a discovery that would change life in the S.U.N as we know it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: She had built a machine that carefully extracted a heat unit and could extract triple the amount of light and heat they normally produce.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: She brought it to the council thinking they'd be excited she found a better way to extract light and heat, but she was wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: The council hid your mother's discovery and exiled her from the Core, forcing her to live in the outskirts.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: When I found out I rushed to help her and was discharged from the enforcers and exiled, just for association.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: *Kip pauses to take a breath*

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: So, we started a life out here together.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara told me she was caught trying to steal some of the lab equipment...

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: It wasn't until the day she found out she was pregnant with you she told me the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara knew that with you coming into this world she had to do something to make it better.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We planned for months on the best way to leak your mother's discovery to the public, without getting killing in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While we were working you decided you wanted to come into the world early-- you were always this stubborn.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: After a long labour you were born, and Clara got to hold you for the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I could see it in her face that she would do anything to get her discovery to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While fetching Clara a drink down the hall, I saw two man suddenly and swiftly wheel her out of the room.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I started into a sprint, screaming for her but heard no answer.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: The men turned into a room not too far down the hall, but when I ran in, it was empty.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I never forgave myself for leaving her alone in that room.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: That was the last time anyone saw her.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: She made a life-changing discovery, and they hid it?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: We must finish what she started! Where's the machine?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Woah, woah, slow down. I have no idea what happened to the machine.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: We can find it!

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I'm not sure if you're ready for this. You have no idea what you are going up against.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: These people don't care at all about you and won't think twice about killing you.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I might not know what I'm up against, but you do.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I don't know where to start, I need your help Kip, please.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: *sighs*

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This is all your mother's stuff... Or rather, what's left of it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While in the hospital that night, enforcers raided our house and took almost everything.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Thankfully for us, we had a few boxes hidden.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I can't believe this has been here the whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Is this her journal?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yes, it is. Clara used to write all her important notes in there.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What happened to these pages?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We used to rip out pages and plaster them to the walls while working with them...

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I guess those were taken when they raided the place.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: They could be anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Mrs. Watts? Isn't that the old lady that lives in our district?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yeah, your mother and her used to chat all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Perfect! It looks like we found our first lead.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: There's no time to waste, we have to speak with her.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Calm down, we're in the grey zone right now.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: There are enforcers everywhere telling people to stay in their houses.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I can go by myself. It'll be faster, and I can sneak past the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I can't believe I'm agreeing to this.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Remember you NEVER want to get caught out in the midnight zone. There are enforcers, bandits, and things...

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: ...you could never imagine, yes, I know. You've been telling me the same thing since I was a little kid.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Because I never want you to forget.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira, please be careful, and good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I'll see you soon.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Alright, it's not that far. Lira, you can do this.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Not a single light on...

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Let me try the back.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Mrs. Watts it's me Lira Drave.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I have something important to talk to you about.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: It's about my mom, Clara.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: What are you doing out? You might've been seen.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Now what is so urgent you couldn't wait for light?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I found out the truth about my mom. About her discovery...

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Shhh! Don't say that too loud or you'll get us both killed.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: ...and about how she disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I believe that I can finish her work, and you are the only lead I had.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I need to find her machine.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I haven't thought about Clara in years. We used to worl in the tower together until...

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Well you know what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Do you know anything about the machine ashe created?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Of course! I helped her make it.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: She did most of the work, I just assisted in the places she struggled.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Do you know where it is?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: No, I'm afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: The last I heard is that someone split it up into three parts.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Three parts?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Hold on one second.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Now, are you sure you want to be a part of this?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Once you start, there is no going back.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yes!

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I'm hesitant but you're Clara's daughter and if anyone was ready for this it'd be her own.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Please, I promise I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Here are the three parts.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: So, do you know where any of the parts are?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Well... I don't know where they are, but I might know someone who does.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Who?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: There is an antique shop across the street, owned by a man nammed Darren. He knew your mom well.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: So, he shouldn't have a hard time recognizing who you are.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: All you have to do is get across the street without being seen.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: And hurry, the midnight zone is approaching.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: They're not moving, how am I supposed to get by?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I left some rocks out front. You can use those to distract the enforcers.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll go now and make it quick.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Be smart Lira and be careful who you trust.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Now how do I get in?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Hopefully my luck stays like this.
